questions.question: What is the difference between pure and impure pipes in Angular?
questions.title: Pure vs Impure Pipes in Angular — Performance Explained
questions.direct_answer:
What is the difference between pure and impure pipes in Angular?

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the framework runtime (render, reconciliation, DI, CD) and the browser), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** Pure (default) recomputes only when input reference changes; impure recomputes every change detection cycle; impure pipes can hurt perf.

**Classic weak answer:** Writing an impure pipe that does heavy work — it runs every CD cycle; prefer a component property with reactive updates.

**Senior finish:** Mention the async pipe is technically impure (subscribes to Observable) but highly optimized; it handles unsubscription automatically.

sections.title: Why this question matters
sections.content:
This question — **Pure vs Impure Pipes in Angular — Performance Explained** — shows up constantly in **frontend / fullstack** interviews because it separates candidates who memorized docs from candidates who can **reason about real systems**.

**Restate the prompt:** What is the difference between pure and impure pipes in Angular?

A gold-level answer does four things in order:

1. **Define** the terms in plain English (what it is / what problem it solves).
2. **Explain the mechanism** (what runs when: browser, bundler, framework, network).
3. **Compare trade-offs** (speed vs correctness vs security vs DX) with **when you would not use** the default.
4. **Ground it in production** — caching, auth, observability, tests, or an incident you handled.

Interviewers are listening for: **Pure (default) recomputes only when input reference changes; impure recomputes every change detection cycle; impure pipes can hurt perf**.

The fastest way to lose points is: **Writing an impure pipe that does heavy work — it runs every CD cycle; prefer a component property with reactive updates**.

If you only add one “senior” layer, make it: **Mention the async pipe is technically impure (subscribes to Observable) but highly optimized; it handles unsubscription automatically**.

sections.title: Deep dive — what to say
sections.content:
### What to explain (middle of the answer)

- **Core mechanics:** Pure (default) recomputes only when input reference changes; impure recomputes every change detection cycle; impure pipes can hurt perf
- **Concrete shape:** give a small code or config snippet *only if it clarifies* (5–15 lines max).
- **Interviewer follow-ups:** expect “what breaks in production?”, “how do you debug?”, “what would you measure?” — answer them proactively.

### How to sound senior (without rambling)

- Tie the feature to **user-visible outcomes** (performance, accessibility, security).
- Mention **one failure mode** you have actually seen (race, stale cache, hydration mismatch, flaky test).
- Close with **one decision rule** (“choose X when …; choose Y when …”).

questions.question: What is the async pipe in Angular? Why is it recommended?
questions.title: Angular Async Pipe Explained — Auto-Subscribe & Unsubscribe
questions.direct_answer:
What is the async pipe in Angular? Why is it recommended?

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the framework runtime (render, reconciliation, DI, CD) and the browser), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** Subscribes to Observables/Promises in the template, auto-unsubscribes on destroy, triggers CD on emissions, pairs perfectly with OnPush.

**Classic weak answer:** Subscribing manually in ngOnInit and forgetting to unsubscribe in ngOnDestroy — leaks; async pipe handles this automatically.

**Senior finish:** Show async pipe with OnPush + Signals as the modern trio; mention the *ngFor + async + trackBy combo.

interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Show async pipe with OnPush + Signals as the modern trio; mention the *ngFor + async + trackBy combo
